introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2021. Duration: TWO AND A HALF (2 1/2) HOURS.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.

Questions ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.

Each question that is sub-divided has the sub marks in brackets.

In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.

If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées sans source consultable. Aucune statistique précise n'est avancée sauf mention contraire ; les exemples cités sont des exemples reconnus. Les faits cités sont à faire relire par un géographe avant toute mise en avant.
Points : 6 + 3 + (3 + 2) + (2 + 2 + 2) = 20, conformes au sujet (7c : 5 ; 7d : 6). Le « (6marks) » imprimé en 7(a) est transcrit « (6 marks) ».

Fond de carte 7(a) : même feuille que pour la question 6 ; positions décrites, non cartographiées. 7(b) : la réponse dépend de la région choisie en (a)(ii) ; le corrigé traite la région de l'Est et donne une variante pour l'Adamaoua.

Faits à faire vérifier : Dja (réserve de faune) et Korup (parc national) comme réserves forestières ; pétrole offshore du bassin du Rio del Rey (Sud-Ouest) et au large de Kribi ; barrages de Lom Pangar, Memve'ele et Nachtigal ; projets miniers cités (fer de Mbalam, bauxite de Minim-Martap et Ngaoundal, cobalt-nickel de l'Est) ; « Vision 2035 » et programme de logements sociaux cités sans date ni chiffre.

questions.corrige_markdown:
Mark each place with a **dot or symbol**, **name it** and add a **key**. (1 mark each; two for the first item.) The positions are approximate (north at the top):

1. **Bamenda and Buea:** both are in the **west** of the country, near the Nigerian border. **Bamenda** is the capital of the North-West region, in the western highlands (the Bamenda Highlands). **Buea** is the capital of the South-West region, on the south-east slope of **Mount Cameroon**, close to the Atlantic coast, **south of Bamenda**.
2. **One area of sparse population:** the **East region** (the south-eastern forest area); or the Adamawa plateau and the Benue valley. Shade it and label "Sparsely populated (East region)".
3. **A forest reserve:** the **Dja Faunal Reserve**, in the south (the south of the Centre and East regions, near the Dja river); or **Korup National Park** in the far south-west, near the border with Nigeria.
4. **One international airport:** **Douala International Airport** (on the coast, Littoral); or Yaounde-Nsimalen (Centre), or Garoua in the north.
5. **An area where petroleum is mined:** the **south-west coast** (the Rio del Rey basin offshore from Limbe and Ndian, in the South-West region); also off **Kribi** in the south.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Give **TWO** reasons for the low population density in the region marked in **a (ii)**.

(3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
*(Answer for the East region of Cameroon, the area chosen in (a)(ii).)*

1. **Dense equatorial forest and poor soils:** the thick forest is difficult to clear, and the heavy rain leaches the soil of its minerals, so the soils are of low fertility and farming supports few people.
2. **Poor accessibility and few developments:** the region is far from the coast and the big cities, with poor roads and railways and few towns, industries, schools and hospitals, so few people settle and many migrate to the cities; disease (malaria, sleeping sickness) and low economic activity also discourage settlement.

(If the Adamawa plateau or another area was chosen: poor, thin soils and a long dry season, grazing as the main activity, cattle rearing needing few people, and weak transport links.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) Describe **TWO** problems common to Cameroon towns today.

(ii) State the attempts made by government to solve these problems.

(3 + 2 = 5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Two problems common to Cameroon towns (3 marks).**

1. **Housing shortage and unplanned settlements (slums):** the population grows faster than the supply of houses, so many people build in unplanned, overcrowded quarters, often on swampy or steep land, without proper roads, water, electricity and sewers; such areas flood or have landslides in the rainy season.
2. **Traffic congestion, poor waste disposal and sanitation:** roads are narrow, old and crowded with vehicles and motorcycle taxis, and rubbish and drainage are poorly managed, causing floods, pollution and disease; unemployment and the growth of the informal sector are also common.

**(ii) Attempts by the Government (2 marks).**

- **Urban planning and housing:** master plans for the main cities, the demolition and resettlement of houses built in risky places, and a **social housing programme**.
- **Infrastructure and services:** building and tarring roads, drains, bypasses and bridges, supplying water and electricity, waste collection, and **decentralisation** (the councils manage towns) and the development of other towns and growth poles to ease the pressure on Douala and Yaounde.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) "Cameroon will become an emergent state by the year 2035". How is the Government of Cameroon preparing for this in the following sectors?

**(i) Manufacturing industries (ii) Energy (iii) Minerals**

(2+2+2 = 6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Government's plan (the **Vision 2035**, carried out through successive growth and development strategies) is to make Cameroon an **emerging, industrialising country**. In each sector:

**(i) Manufacturing industries (2 marks).** It encourages **industrialisation and local processing** of raw materials (wood, cocoa, cotton, rubber, agricultural products) instead of exporting them raw; it creates **industrial zones and parks** and the **Kribi deep-sea port and industrial complex**; it supports small and medium-sized enterprises, gives investment incentives and improves roads and ports.

**(ii) Energy (2 marks).** It builds more **hydroelectric dams** (for example Lom Pangar, Memve'ele and Nachtigal) and **gas-fired power stations** (Kribi), develops **solar** power in the north, extends the electricity grid, and promotes private investment, in order to give industries and homes a cheap, reliable supply.

**(iii) Minerals (2 marks).** It reforms the **mining code**, carries out geological surveys, and licences companies to develop large deposits (for example iron ore at Mbalam, bauxite at Minim-Martap and Ngaoundal, cobalt and nickel in the East region, and diamond and gold), builds the roads and railways needed to export them, and encourages the processing of minerals in the country.
